units.translation: Lord Apollo, a prophet who was truthful before.
Apollo – the prophet.
Even a bad prophet would know these things.
He sits as the fourth prophet on the throne.
Then I, a prophet, sit down on the throne.
Being a prophet.
Did the prophet instruct you to kill your mother?
But being a prophet, I will not lie.

And this night which you speak of, on the shield – perhaps he would become a prophet of what he will suffer. Thus I emended the interpolated reading in M, μάντις ἡ ἄνοιά τινι [a prophet, the folly to someone].
A prophet, the fear from dreams.

Such a favor – a godless woman, seeking, sends me. Schol. Seeking.
Seeking to bring about death.

But the sound of this double whip reaches me. Thus Robortellus. μαράγμης [of the whip] (with gloss μάστιγος [of the whip]) M. Thus μάστιγι διπλῇ [with a double whip] Ag. 642, Soph. Ai. 110, and μάλθλητα δίγονον [soft double] fr. 137.

Mardus, a Persian proper name
Mardus, a Persian proper name

And fifth (king of the Persians) Mardus ruled. Where the corrector wrote ος διορθωτής ις [the corrector wrote ις] above the letters, adding this scholium: the reading is erroneous; for no one called the magus who attacked the rule of Cambyses Mardus, neither as a family nor as a name. Perhaps then one should write "Μάρδις αἰσχύνη πάτρα [Mardis, shame of the fatherland]." He is the same as the one called Smerdis by Herodotus. Rutgersius in Var. Lect. 3, 10 p. 321 is undoubtedly right in reading Μέρδις [Merdis], which could be said for metrical reasons instead of Σμέρδις [Smerdis], and the scholiast too perhaps wrote that, not Μάρδις [Mardis].
